subject: Follow-up: Skyport security/discovery — authorization & support entitlements
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@skyport.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call + follow-ups (Skyport)

Hi Laura — great speaking earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and three asks to keep momentum: 

1) PII & retention: you mentioned Skyport retains customer transcripts for 180 days for troubleshooting. Can you confirm whether that applies to: 
  - user-supplied prompt text,
  - attachments parsed by the model, and
  - derived embeddings?

2) Support access model: you flagged that support must not have standing access to decrypted payloads. Can you confirm whether break-glass is handled by: temporary JIT elevation logged to an audit trail, or by a separate secure proxy? Any examples of the justification workflow would help.

3) Residency & logging: need to confirm region constraints (US only?) and minimum log retention for access audit (we typically see 1–3 years requested by enterprise SOC teams).

I've attached a short controls checklist and our RBAC matrix prototype to make it easier to map requirements to our configuration. Proposed next step: 30-min handoff with your security lead + our infra engineer next Tues 10–10:30 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Skyport_Requested_Controls_Checklist.pdf (pdf), redwood-rbac-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Laura Chen <laura@skyport.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@skyport.com, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@skyport.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call + follow-ups (Skyport)

Thanks Alex — appreciate the notes and the artifacts. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: we currently keep raw prompts and any uploaded attachments (for model inference) for 180 days; embeddings (derived vectors) are retained for 365 days for analytics. We redacted direct identifiers from stored prompts as part of ingestion where possible, but we still treat raw prompts as PII when they contain sensitive fields.

- Support access / break-glass: we require Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation provisioned via our internal ticketing tool (we use PagerHawk); engineers can request a temporary session (max 2 hours) and every session is recorded. Break-glass requests require an approved ticket with business justification and are reviewed post-mortem by security. We can share a sanitized example flow if helpful.

- Residency: primary constraint is US-East only for this PoC. For full production we may need multi-region with EU option.

- Logging: SOC asked for 24 months for auth/access audit logs and 12 months for application-level request logs; we can be flexible on request logs if they include sampled request IDs rather than full payloads.

We can do Tue 10 PT — looping in our security SME Rajiv and the security mailbox to prep.

Laura Chen
Head of Platform Security
Skyport Systems

Alex / Ben — Rajiv here (security engineering). A few technical questions that we'd like to cover in the Tue handoff so our GRC folks can sign off: 

1) Encryption & key management: is customer data at rest encrypted with a customer-provided KMS key (BYOK) option? If not, what are the controls for key segregation per-tenant?

2) RBAC granularity: can Redwood map support engineers to roles that restrict: 
   - visibility into raw payloads,
   - ability to initiate KV cache restores or snapshot exports, and
   - permission to trigger model-rollbacks?

3) Audit evidence: what logs do you surface for break-glass sessions (session start/stop, requesting user, justification text, privileged commands executed)? We need to confirm the format (syslog vs JSON events) and retention APIs.

If you have sample logs and a quick diagram of the support elevation flow it will save time on our side.

—Rajiv
Security Engineer
Skyport Systems
